messages:
Jordan: Heads-up — customer VeloxHealth is pushing for a stricter p99 target than we expected. They want p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 300ms at sustained 100 QPS for their chat route.
Maya: That's tighter than the deal we previewed. Do we have a technical plan to hit that without blowing cost?
Sam: Quick note: our recent kernel swap (fused_gemm_v2) improved mean and p95 in most workloads but I measured a p99 regression on long-context chat profiles.
Jordan: Can you paste numbers?
Sam: Sure — short snippet from local perf runs:
```
profile summary (baseline -> after kernel v2):
- p50: 45ms -> 38ms
- p95: 92ms -> 110ms
- p99: 210ms -> 360ms
- sustained QPS: 100
```
Sam: The p99 tail widened for sequences >1024 tokens, likely due to worse KV cache hot-path codegen.
Igor: I can dig into the kernel codegen differences. My initial hunch: vectorized gather path introduced occasional scalar fallback for certain sequence alignments.
Liam: From sales: VeloxHealth signed for an enterprise SKU; they'll expect firm commitments. If we can't meet p99 we need to offer a fallback (discount or dedicated capacity).
Maya: Product ask: give options with tradeoffs (cost, throughput, complexity) by EOB today so sales can push back.
Dana: Ops note — if we attempt microbatch tuning, we need to ensure we don't violate resource limits on their Dedicated pool. Also need tracing hooks to detect KV warmup misses.
Jordan: Proposed options: 1) Microbatch small (2) + kernel fallback to safe_fp32 on tail cases 2) Keep current kernel + aggressive KV warmup + prefix caching 3) Offer Dedicated with reserved capacity + microbatch=1 for strict p99.
Sam: Numbers from perf bench for options (approx):
- Option 1 (microbatch=2 + fallback): p95 ~115ms, p99 ~280ms, throughput ~85 QPS equivalent, cost +10%
- Option 2 (current kernel + kv warmup): p95 ~120ms, p99 ~330ms, throughput ~95 QPS, cost +5%
- Option 3 (dedicated microbatch=1): p95 ~100ms, p99 ~250ms, throughput limited to 70 QPS per GPU but stable, cost +35% (reserved)
Igor: For Option 1 I can implement a fast path patch to avoid scalar fallback; will take ~2 days to validate but could reduce p99 further.
Liam: Sales preference is Option 3 if engineering thinks it's the only way to guarantee p99 SLA. Customers will accept price if SLA is tight.
Maya: We should present a recommended default (Option 1) with an Escalation Plan to move to Option 3 if tail doesn't improve after kernel patch.
Jordan: Agree. Also suggest automated routing policy: route->if p99 spikes > 10% over baseline then switch route to dedicated variant and notify oncall.
Dana: I'll add tracing for `kv_cache_miss` and a p99 spike alert. Need the metric name. Sam / Igor can you expose `runtime.kv.hot_miss_rate`?
Igor: Yep, will add metric and a histogram for sequence-length buckets.
Sam: I'll run a controlled canary - perf harness against 10k long-context requests with the microbatch=2 + fallback setup and kv warmup enabled. Will post dashboard link.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for route `velox-chat` with config `microbatch=2,kernel_policy=primary:fused_gemm_v2,fallback:safe_fp32,kv_warmup=true`.
Jordan: Thanks. Action items recap: 1) Igor - investigate codegen scalar fallback (2d) 2) Sam - run 10k canary and share dashboard (EOD) 3) Dana - add kv_hot_miss metric + p99 alert rule (today) 4) Maya/Liam - present options to customer with recommended default + escalation.
Maya: I'll draft language for the customer message and include the three options + estimated cost deltas.
Liam: I'll coordinate contract language for optional Dedicated carve-out.
Dana: I'll add dashboard panels for quick ops view and wire alerts to #eng-oncall.
Sam: Canary results uploading -> short link: https://perf.local/d/velox/canary-194567 (will update with numbers).
Jordan: If canary shows p99 <= 300ms we're in negotiation land. If not, fallback plan ready.
Maya: High-level decision: recommend Option 1 now, with target: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms, and automatic failover to Dedicated if triggers persist 15m.
Liam: Sounds good. I'll flag to VeloxHealth that we can achieve target contingent on the kernel patch & canary.
Igor: Will post a PR with the micro-optimization and perf numbers once I reproduce locally.
Sam: ack, will monitor and post final canary numbers here. :thumbsup:
Jordan: Great work team. Keep updates short in-thread.
Maya: Thanks everyone — I'll own the customer comms.
Liam: TY.
deploy-bot: Canary complete — 1/4 nodes healthy, 3/4 reporting increased p99. See dashboard: https://perf.local/d/velox/canary-194567
Sam: Noted — looks like fallback path triggered on 3 nodes. Investigating divergence now.
Jordan: Ok team, reconvene if new numbers change the recommendation.
Maya: We'll schedule a quick sync with VeloxEngineering tomorrow morning if needed.
